explanation: Pointing directly at a person with your index finger is widely used in Spain but can come across as blunt or aggressive, especially when aimed at someone during a disagreement — soft etiquette advice favors gesturing with an open hand instead. Unlike in East Asia, there's no strong, well-documented taboo against it, so it's more a matter of manners than a hard rule.
local_tip: When indicating a person, use an open hand rather than a single finger, especially with someone you don't know well.

also_check.note: Pointing with a single finger is considered impolite; gesturing with an open hand is the norm.
Pointing with the index finger is seen as offensive; people often point with the thumb instead.
Pointing with the index finger is common and unremarkable in everyday casual conversation.

sources.title: Insider's Guide to Understanding Spanish Hand Gestures
